extracted.intended_audience: general readers; writers and literary professionals researching Tin House (prospective contributors, students, librarians)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia profile of Tin House, an American literary magazine and book publisher, summarizing its history, editorial focus, programs, staff, and publications. Useful for writers or researchers wanting an overview of the magazine's scope, reputation, and offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content types published
rubrics_metrics.description: Tin House published fiction, essays, and poetry, as well as interviews with important literary figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine's scope included standard literary forms (fiction, essays, poetry) plus interviews; this indicates the kinds of submissions and editorial attention the publication gave to those genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special sections and series (editorial programming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Included recurring sections such as a 'Lost and Found' section dedicated to exceptional and generally overlooked books, 'Readable Feast' food writing features, and 'Literary Pilgrimages' about visits to the homes of writing greats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These named features illustrate the magazine's editorial interests and potential niches for submissions (e.g., food writing, literary-history pieces, recovered/rediscovered works).

rubrics_metrics.name: New Voices / support for previously unpublished writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Tin House was distinguished from many other notable literary magazines by actively seeking work from previously unpublished writers to feature as 'New Voices'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorially prioritized discovery and promotion of emerging writers; relevant to submission strategy for first-time or previously-unpublished authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop program — admission and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Tin House ran a by-admission-only summer writers' workshop held at Reed College.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshop was selective (admission-only), suggesting competitive entry and a program-oriented facet of the Tin House ecosystem (education/networking) separate from magazine submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book publishing arm (Tin House Books)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2005 Tin House expanded into the book division, Tin House Books, publishing novels, story collections, anthologies, nonfiction, and other titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The existence of a book division signals additional publishing pathways (book contracts, reprints, curated anthologies) and a broader editorial program beyond the magazine; the page lists many book titles and authors as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial leadership and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Key staff listed include Publisher and Editor-in-Chief Win McCormack, Editor Rob Spillman, Art Director Diane Chonette, Deputy Publisher Holly Macarthur, Managing Editor Cheston Knapp, and other editors and designers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named editors and roles provide insight into editorial taste, institutional continuity, and points of contact; recognition of senior editors can inform expectations about editorial standards and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and operational status
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency: Quarterly. First issue 1999; Tin House announced closing its literary magazine after 20 years (final issue June 2019) to focus on books and workshops. Tin House Books was later acquired by Zando (March 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the magazine's historical cadence and that the print magazine ceased in 2019, which is essential context for submissions, archival research, or assessing current opportunities with the brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial prestige and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Tin House was honored by major American literary awards and anthologies; examples include a Summer 2003 story featured in The Best American Short Stories 2004 and a story noted as a 'juror favorite' in The O. Henry Prize Stories 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past anthology inclusions and award recognition signal editorial quality and prestige—useful when evaluating the magazine's reputation or the impact of publication there on a writer's career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of contributors and notable authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine and books published work by a wide range of established and emerging writers (the page lists many contributors such as Alice Munro, Stephen King, Deborah Eisenberg, David Foster Wallace, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A diverse roster of high-profile contributors demonstrates the magazine's reach and the types of voices and caliber of work it printed; helpful for benchmarking submissions.
